description: Does capability scale predictably and indefinitely with compute? This is a foundational factual dispute between Accelerationists and Safetyists/Skeptics.

instances.assertion: Placeholder instance. Add real document instances as sources are ingested.
Scaling compute and algorithmic efficiency consistently improves model performance.
The document estimates that AI will increase total factor productivity (TFP) by no more than 0.66% over 10 years.
The 'No Free Lunch' theorem states that no single machine learning algorithm works best for every problem, implying that specialization is necessary for optimal performance.
As model size increases, language modeling ability (lms) increases, and correspondingly its stereotypical score (ss).
Scaling laws observed in current AI models will continue to hold for future, larger models, suggesting that increased compute leads to higher intelligence.
